title: General directed stage pairs and their supplied exact and shift data
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder (a set in an arbitrary universe), and let $C_i$ be categories, with their object and morphism universes fixed independently of that of $I$. A stage system $S$ consists of functors $T_{ij}:C_i\to C_j$ for $i\le j$ and natural isomorphisms $a_{ijk}:T_{jk}T_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{ik}$ satisfying
$$a_{ikl}\circ T_{kl}(a_{ijk})=a_{ijl}\circ(a_{jkl})_{T_{ij}}\quad(i\le j\le k\le l).$$
There is no specified unitor and no requirement $T_{ii}=1$. Write $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ for its pair category. Its objects are $(i,x)$ with $x\in C_i$. A representative from $(i,x)$ to $(j,y)$ is $(m,u)$ with $m\ge i,j$ and $u:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y$. Transport to $n\ge m$ is
$$u_n=a_{jmn,y}\circ T_{mn}(u)\circ a_{imn,x}^{-1}.$$
Morphisms are representatives modulo equality after transport to a common upper stage; composition is represented by composition at a common stage. The identity at $(i,x)$ is $[i,1_{T_{ii}x}]$. The inclusion $j_i:C_i\to P$ sends $x$ to $(i,x)$ and $f$ to $[i,T_{ii}(f)]$. Write $\theta_{ij}:j_jT_{ij}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_i$ for the canonical identification whose component at $x$ is represented at $j$ by $a_{ijj,x}$, and write $\delta_{(i,x),m}=\theta_{im,x}^{-1}:(i,x)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_m(T_{im}x)$.

An exact-stage pair datum means such $S$, together with pretriangulated structures on the $C_i$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], and fixed preadditive, zero-object and integer-shift structures on $P$, all integer-shift functors being additive. Each $j_i$ is supplied as additive and with natural shift comparisons $\beta_{i,n,x}:j_i(x[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(j_ix)[n]$. Each $T_{ij}$ is supplied with comparisons $\sigma_{ij,n,x}:T_{ij}(x[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T_{ij}x)[n]$ and is exact. Both families of comparisons respect the shift-zero and shift-add isomorphisms. The given $\theta_{ij}$ commute with these comparisons: for every integer $n$,
$$\beta_{i,n,x}\circ\theta_{ij,x[n]}=\theta_{ij,x}[n]\circ\beta_{j,n,T_{ij}x}\circ j_j(\sigma_{ij,n,x}).$$
No pretriangulation of $P$ is part of these data. For a triangle $U=(x\xrightarrow f y\xrightarrow g z\xrightarrow h x[1])$ of $C_i$, define
$$j_i^\triangle U=(j_ix\xrightarrow{j_if}j_iy\xrightarrow{j_ig}j_iz\xrightarrow{\beta_{i,1,x}\circ j_ih}(j_ix)[1]).$$
Triangles and triangle isomorphisms mean [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. Define the common-stage predicate
$$D_S(V)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists i\in I\ \exists U\in\operatorname{Triangle}(C_i),\quad U\text{ is distinguished and }V\cong j_i^\triangle U.$$
